index.cell_alerts_h: It tells you before you hit it
index.cell_alerts_p:
At 80% and 95% out of the box, or whichever levels you set instead — once per
           crossing, not once per poll.
index.cell_keychain_p:
Credentials stay in the keychain, never copied into preferences or logs. When something
           fails, the app sends a description of the failure to its author, stripped of paths,
           addresses and anything token-shaped before it leaves the machine — and it can be
           switched off. The only other request is a daily check for a new version, and that can
           be switched off too.
index.cell_langs_p:
Including Arabic, laid out right to left. Switching takes effect immediately, with no
           restart.
index.cell_quiet_p: Nothing arrives while you sleep, and nothing is delivered late to make up for it.
index.cell_timer_h: A timer in the menu bar
index.cell_timer_p:
Whichever limit is closest to running out, and how long until it frees up — without
           clicking. The strip can carry the countdown, the percentage, both, or just the icon,
           and a shortcut of your choosing opens the window without reaching for the mouse.
index.cell_widgets_p:
All four sizes on macOS; on iPhone the home screen and the lock screen. The same
           account row the window uses, so they cannot drift apart.
index.chart_aria: A month of weekly limits for three accounts: curves climbing between resets, with notification thresholds marked at 80 and 95 percent.
index.fact_adding_d:
Choose Claude Code or OpenAI Codex, then sign in with OAuth and PKCE in your own
            browser. Local CLI accounts are also detected.
index.fact_claude_d: Live, from the OAuth usage endpoint.
index.fact_codex_d:
Live usage for browser accounts. Local session files are watched with FSEvents,
            with snapshot age shown.
index.fact_core_d:
A Swift package with no AppKit and no human-facing strings. Window, widgets and phone
            share one row view.
index.fact_cost_d:
One request per Claude account per poll. Five minutes apart in the background, once
            a minute with the window open — or anywhere between thirty seconds and an hour, if you
            set it. Claude name and plan are asked once and kept for six hours. Each saved Codex account
            adds one usage request per poll; local Codex readings come from disk.
index.fact_deps_d: None. Every import is either Apple's own framework or a module of this project.
index.fact_notyet_d:
Cursor, GitHub Copilot and Gemini CLI. A provider that cannot be checked against a
            live account would quietly show zero, which is worse than nothing.
index.fact_requires_d: macOS 14 or later. The iPhone app needs iOS 17.

index.plans_p1:
Your keychain holds a token only for the plan you are signed into, and refreshing it can
      rotate that token on the server — signing Claude Code out. A monitor that logs you out of the
      thing it monitors is worse than none.
index.plans_p2: So the active account is read-only here, and Softcap keeps its own copy of the refresh token for when you move on with /login. It can only take that copy while Softcap is running, so sign into each plan the ordinary way with the app open — one poll later it is kept, and they stay on screen together. Reading the CLI's keychain item needs macOS's permission, which Softcap asks for when you press a button — never from a timer nobody is watching.

index.time_caption: The dashed guides are where notifications fire: a nudge at 80%, a last warning at 95%. Every drop is a week's allowance renewing. And a break, like alex's, is a stretch with nothing measured; drawing across it would claim a reading nobody took.
index.time_lede: One line per account. Colour means which account here and how loaded everywhere else, so the two scales never borrow from each other. The plans renew on different days — so at any hour, the picture says which account is fresh.

index.under_title: For the sort of person who reads this part
index.why_p1:
Softcap reads subscription usage directly for accounts added through the browser.
      These requests fetch limits without sending a prompt or running a model.
index.why_p2: Local Codex accounts also work: the CLI writes its readings into ~/.codex/sessions, and Softcap watches those files. A reading from a file is a snapshot, so every surface shows when it was taken. Sign into that account through Softcap's browser flow to see current usage independently of the CLI.
